sentences: Presburger arithmetic describes integers using addition and order without unrestricted multiplication.
The saved question asks whether adding a predicate for prime numbers preserves decidability.
The added predicate imports number-theoretic structure that the base arithmetic language cannot directly express.
An answer would mark a sharp boundary between a tame linear theory and richer arithmetic reasoning.

The excerpt attributes this question to its source but does not specify the integer-domain convention or provide a current progress audit, so the draft keeps the decisional target separate from later-status claims.
